ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Colliding Conducting Slab A thin conducting square slab with side length $s=5 \mathrm{~cm}$, initial charge $q=0.1 \mu \mathrm{C}$, and mass $m=100 \mathrm{~g}$ is given a kick and sent bouncing between two infinite conducting plates separated by a distance $d=0.5 \mathrm{~cm} \ll s$ and with surface charge density $\pm \sigma= \pm 50 \mu \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$. After a long time it is observed exactly in the middle of the two plates to be traveling with velocity of magnitude $v=3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and direction $\theta=30^{\circ}$ with respect to the horizontal line parallel to the plates. How many collisions occur after it has traveled a distance $L=15 \mathrm{~m}$ horizontally from when it was last observed? Assume that all collisions are elastic, and neglect induced charges. Note that the setup is horizontal so gravity does not need to be accounted for.

method.method_draft: Use an unfolded-trajectory kinematics model. From the image, identify the two horizontal charged plates, the slab initially at the midplane, the separation d, and the velocity making angle theta above the horizontal; the first hit is toward the upper plate if using the drawn direction. From the text, take s=0.05 m, d=0.005 m, sigma=50e-6 C/m^2, m=0.100 kg, v=3 m/s, theta=30 deg, and L=15 m. After many contacts, ignore the initial charge because each conducting collision resets the slab charge to the sign of the plate with magnitude Q=sigma s^2. The electric field between plates is E=sigma/epsilon0, so the magnitude of the vertical acceleration after each collision is a=QE/m=sigma^2 s^2/(epsilon0 m), always along the slab's vertical motion after unfolding the bounces. The horizontal speed is constant vx=v cos theta, so the observation-to-finish time is T=L/vx. The unfolded vertical path length covered in that time is R=(v sin theta)T+0.5 a T^2. Collisions occur when the unfolded vertical path reaches d/2, d/2+d, d/2+2d, ...; therefore N=floor((R-d/2)/d)+1. Substituting epsilon0≈8.85e-12 gives N=25273.

method.method_draft: Use an event-index/energy-threshold calculation. From the image, note that the slab starts at the midpoint between the plates and must travel a vertical distance d/2 to the first plate, then distance d between every subsequent collision. From the text, read the same parameters and compute vx=v cos theta and initial vertical speed u0=v sin theta. After long-time conducting contacts, take the slab's charge after each collision as alternating sign with magnitude Q=sigma s^2; because the plate field is E=sigma/epsilon0, the force after each rebound accelerates the slab away from the plate with magnitude a=sigma^2 s^2/(epsilon0 m). For the nth future collision, the vertical path length accumulated since observation is ell_n=d/2+(n-1)d. By work-energy/constant-acceleration kinematics, the time to accumulate path length ell_n is t_n=(sqrt(u0^2+2a ell_n)-u0)/a. The total available time before the slab has moved horizontally L is T=L/(v cos theta). Find the largest integer n satisfying t_n<=T, equivalently d/2+(n-1)d <= u0 T + (1/2)aT^2. Evaluating with epsilon0≈8.85e-12 yields n=25273.

A thin conducting slab of horizontal size s lies between them, and its velocity arrow v points up and to the right, with the horizontal direction parallel to the plates. Since the slab is observed at the midpoint, the first future collision requires vertical travel d/2, while every later collision requires vertical travel d. Reasoning: Convert the data: s = 0.05 m, d = 0.005 m, σ = 50e-6 C/m^2 = 5.0e-5 C/m^2, m = 0.100 kg, v = 3 m/s, θ = 30 degrees, L = 15 m. The horizontal speed is vx = v cos θ = 3 cos 30° = 2.598 m/s, so the time available to travel horizontally 15 m is T = L/vx = 15/2.598 = 5.7735 s. The initial vertical speed magnitude is u0 = v sin θ = 3 sin 30° = 1.5 m/s. After long-time conducting contacts, use the method assumption that the slab charge after each collision alternates sign with magnitude Q = σs^2. The electric field magnitude between the plates is E = σ/ε0, so the vertical acceleration magnitude away from each plate is a = QE/m = σ^2 s^2/(ε0 m). With ε0 ≈ 8.85e-12, a = (5.0e-5)^2(0.05)^2 / ((8.85e-12)(0.100)) ≈ 7.06 m/s^2. Treating the accumulated vertical path length as motion with initial speed u0 and acceleration a, the vertical path length covered in time T is ell = u0 T + 0.5 a T^2 ≈ 1.5(5.7735) + 0.5(7.062)(5.7735)^2 ≈ 126.363 m. The nth future collision occurs after vertical path ell_n = d/2 + (n - 1)d. Thus d/2 + (n - 1)d <= ell, so n <= floor((ell - d/2)/d) + 1 = floor((126.363 - 0.0025)/0.005) + 1 = floor(25272.04) + 1 = 25273.
